Canonical timeseries error codes.

detaileddescription.para: Codes in range [400, 499] are timeseries-specific. Codes in range [400, 419] are Phase 1-2 error codes. Codes in range [410, 445] are Phase 3 error codes (new in Phase 3).

Phase 3 adds incident-specific codes for:
Ingest path: BUFFER_PRESSURE, BUFFER_OVERFLOW, FLUSH_TIMEOUT, etc.
Query path: RANGE_INVALID, RETENTION_BOUNDARY_CROSSED, QUERY_TIMEOUT, etc.
Lifecycle path: RETENTION_POLICY_VIOLATION, DELETION_FAILED, ENCRYPTION_ROTATION_FAILURE, etc.
Integration path: REMOTE_WRITE_FAILURE, REMOTE_WRITE_VALIDATION_ERROR, etc.

briefdescription.para: Requires immediate remediation (data loss, auth failure).

Incident severity classification.

detaileddescription.para:
Severity guides operational response:
CRITICAL: Immediate action required (e.g., data loss risk)
ERROR: Failure that degrades service (e.g., buffer overflow, key rotation)
WARN: Degraded behavior but service continues (e.g., high backpressure)
INFO: Normal operational event (e.g., retention GC, flush completion)

memberdef.name: IncidentHandler

briefdescription.para: Optional callback function for incident handling.

detaileddescription.para: Applications can register an IncidentHandler to receive all emitted incidents for logging, metrics, alerting, or tracing.

briefdescription.para: Result type for TsEdgeCaseHandler operations.

detaileddescription.para: Convention: nullopt = success; non-nullopt = error code.

briefdescription.para: Minimum accepted point timestamp (Unix nanoseconds; 1 ns after epoch).

detaileddescription.para: Maximum accepted point timestamp (approximately year 2554; sentinel for "open end"). Set to INT64_MAX to represent an unbounded open interval end.
Maximum number of out-of-order points buffered per series before a forced re-sort flush is triggered.

briefdescription.para: Minimum accepted downsampling resolution in nanoseconds (1 µs).
Maximum number of series in a single TSStore instance.
Maximum number of data points per write batch.
Default retention period in seconds (30 days).
Global incident handler pointer (relaxed atomicity, updated rarely).
Returns true when the error code is a non-retryable hard error.
Returns true when the error code indicates a data-lifecycle condition (series not found, retention expired) that the caller should handle distinctly from hard errors.
Returns true when the error code indicates backpressure that writer should handle.

detaileddescription.para: Backpressure errors indicate buffer/queue congestion. Writers should implement exponential backoff or rate limiting.

briefdescription.para: Returns true when the error code is potentially retryable.

detaileddescription.para: Transient errors include buffer congestion, timeouts, and remote errors.

briefdescription.para: Returns a human-readable string for the given severity.
Returns true when the ingest error is unrecoverable (not worth retry).
Returns true when backpressure should be applied to writer.
Returns true when the query error is unrecoverable.
Returns true when the error indicates missing data but query is valid.
Returns true when lifecycle error is unrecoverable.
Returns true when lifecycle error requires administrative action.
Returns true when integration error is retryable (transient).
Returns true when integration error is non-retryable (permanent).
Registers a global incident handler.

detaileddescription.para: The handler will be called for all incidents emitted by timeseries operations. Only one handler is active at a time; registering a new handler replaces the old one.

parameterdescription.para: Callback function, or nullptr to disable incident reporting.

briefdescription.para: Retrieves the current global incident handler.

simplesect.para: The active handler, or nullptr if none is registered.

briefdescription.para: Emits an incident via the registered handler (if any).

detaileddescription.para: This function has bounded latency and will not throw. It is safe to call from any path (ingest, query, lifecycle, integration).
